Two coders' GToBI labels

Source: R/data.R
tobi_agreement.Rd

Two trained coders label the same 456 words from 40 German utterances with GToBI pitch accents and phrase boundaries: 20 utterances of read and 20 of spontaneous speech. Coders agree on whether a word is accented for about 86% of words and on the exact accent label for about 71%, close to the agreement Grice et al. (1996) report for GToBI. In this simulation, accent agreement is lower in spontaneous speech. For percentage agreement and Cohen's kappa.

Usage

tobi_agreement

Format

A tibble with 456 rows and 8 columns:

utterance

Utterance ID, U01 to U40.

style

"read" or "spontaneous".

word

Word ID (utterance_wNN).

position

Position of the word in the utterance.

accent_1, accent_2

Pitch accent labelled by coder 1 and coder 2: "none", "H*", "L+H*", "L*", "L*+H", "H+!H*" or "H+L*".

boundary_1, boundary_2

Boundary after the word labelled by coder 1 and coder 2: "none", "intermediate" or "intonation phrase".

Source

data-raw/tobi_agreement.R

Details

True model: each word has a true accent (55% none) and boundary (always an intonation phrase boundary at the end of the utterance, 12% intermediate boundaries elsewhere). Each coder gives the true label with probability plogis(base - difficulty), where base is 2.6 for unaccented and 1.6 for accented words (0.2 lower for coder 2) and the word's difficulty has mean 0 in read and 0.5 in spontaneous speech (SD 0.5). Otherwise the coder picks a similar label (e.g. "L+H*" for "H*").

References

Grice, M., Reyelt, M., Benzmüller, R., Mayer, J. & Batliner, A. (1996). Consistency in transcription and labelling of German intonation with GToBI. In Proceedings of the 4th International Conference on Spoken Language Processing (ICSLP 96) (pp. 1716-1719). Philadelphia. doi:10.1109/ICSLP.1996.607958

Grice, M., Baumann, S. & Benzmüller, R. (2005). German intonation in autosegmental-metrical phonology. In S.-A. Jun (ed.), Prosodic Typology: The Phonology of Intonation and Phrasing (pp. 55-83). Oxford: Oxford University Press. doi:10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199249633.003.0003

Pitrelli, J. F., Beckman, M. E. & Hirschberg, J. (1994). Evaluation of prosodic transcription labeling reliability in the ToBI framework. Proceedings of ICSLP 1994. https://www.isca-archive.org/icslp_1994/pitrelli94_icslp.html

Examples

kappa <- function(a, b) {
  tab <- table(a, b)
  po <- sum(diag(tab)) / sum(tab)
  pe <- sum(rowSums(tab) * colSums(tab)) / sum(tab)^2
  c(agreement = po, kappa = (po - pe) / (1 - pe))
}
with(tobi_agreement, kappa(accent_1 != "none", accent_2 != "none"))
#> agreement     kappa 
#> 0.8640351 0.7273148 
with(subset(tobi_agreement, accent_1 != "none" & accent_2 != "none"), kappa(accent_1, accent_2))
#> agreement     kappa 
#> 0.6666667 0.5754880 
sapply(split(tobi_agreement, tobi_agreement$style),
       function(d) kappa(d$accent_1 != "none", d$accent_2 != "none"))
#>                read spontaneous
#> agreement 0.8864629   0.8414097
#> kappa     0.7706118   0.6833785
